fs-wat-clear.front: A creek looks crystal clear. Safe to drink?
fs-wat-clear.back: No. Treat every lake, creek and spring. Germs are invisible.

fs-wat-giardia.back: Giardiasis, a gut infection from the Giardia parasite, mostly from contaminated water.

fs-wat-delay.front: When do Giardia symptoms usually start, and how long do they last?
fs-wat-delay.back: Usually 1 to 3 weeks after infection; they can last 2 to 6 weeks.

fs-wat-boil.back: Rolling boil at least 1 minute; above 2,000 m at least 2 minutes (HealthLink BC).

fs-wat-bleach.front: Bleach dose for 1 litre of clear water?
fs-wat-bleach.back: 2 drops of unscented household bleach, wait 30 minutes.

If the water is cloudy or colder than 10 degrees Celsius, double the dose and wait 1 to 2 hours.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>

fs-wat-bleach-cold.front: Bleach in cloudy or cold (under 10 °C) water?
fs-wat-bleach-cold.back: Double the dose and wait 1 to 2 hours.

fs-wat-chlorine-giardia.back: Generally not effective. Boil or filter for Giardia.

fs-wat-cloudy.back: Strain through cloth, let it settle, pour off the clear water, then treat.

fs-wat-uv.front: Weak spot of a UV pen?
fs-wat-uv.back: Only works in small amounts of clear water. Particles shield germs.

fs-wat-nofix.front: Green scum or a fuel sheen: boil it?
fs-wat-nofix.back: No. Boiling does not remove toxins or chemicals. Find other water.

fs-wat-freeze.front: Why keep the filter warm in November?
fs-wat-freeze.back: Many hollow fibre filters can be damaged by freezing. Check the maker.
